Bloomberg, 9 July 2026: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-09/hormuz-ship-insurance-demand-drops-as-owners-get-nervous
"Shipping Traffic Through Hormuz Slows as Insurance Costs Rise and Caution Grows". London marine insurers seeing fewer inquiries for journeys transiting the Strait of Hormuz; cost of cover had risen.

War-risk premiums (snippet): surged to between 3 per cent and 10 per cent of hull value, up from 0.25 per cent before the war. A $100m tanker now faces war risk premiums of $3m to $10m, versus roughly $250,000 prior to hostilities. [ATTRIBUTION UNCONFIRMED — snippet not tied to an approved outlet]

US Navy-led Joint Maritime Information Center raised its advisory level for transiting Hormuz from "substantial" to "severe", the highest category, citing likelihood of "deliberate hostile action".

Tanker attacks (snippet): Iran struck two UAE supertankers in the strait, killing one sailor and injuring eight. The tankers, Mombasa and Al Bahyah, both operated by Adnoc Logistics and Services, were struck by two Iranian cruise missiles in the southern part of the waterway. [ATTRIBUTION UNCONFIRMED]

Trading Economics: Brent rose to 85.95 USD/Bbl on 17 July 2026, up 2.04% from the previous day. https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil
Brent traded above $84 per barrel on Friday and was on track to gain more than 10% for the week.

EIA: revised Brent forecast down 14% for 2026 after the US-Iran agreement reopened the Strait of Hormuz, to $82/bbl from $95/bbl. https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/

ISW: Only eight vessels transited the strait on 16 July 2026.
